trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide:
This is the platinum, and there is no separate task behind it: it pops the moment you have earned the other 54 trophies. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap, not a trophy to chase on its own. Work the stages in order — story, strangers, activities, collectibles, crime and money, then cleanup — and the platinum will arrive on its own when the last of the 54 lands.

The only trophy that needs a plan of its own is the 100% completion gold, “A Long Road”, since it gathers nearly everything else. Keep the missables page open from the start of your playthrough: the 18 flagged trophies are the only ones that can genuinely cost you a second run.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide:
Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players will earn: just play the story from the start and finish the mission. There is nothing to prepare and nothing to miss — the mission introduces the game and the trophy pops when its final beat plays out.

If you are starting a fresh playthrough for the platinum, this is your warm-up: learn the movement, driving and shooting the mission teaches you, because the same skills carry the whole roadmap.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide:
Play through Chapter 1 to its end. Chapter trophies unlock when the chapter’s last mission finishes, so there is no extra objective and no way to miss this one — finishing the story is the whole requirement.

Use Chapter 1 to get comfortable with Leonida: explore between missions, try a side activity or two, and start noticing the collectible and activity systems, since the later stages of the roadmap ask for a lot of them.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide:
Play through Chapter 2 to its end; the trophy pops when the chapter’s final mission is done. Like every chapter trophy, it cannot be missed — it is a straight reward for finishing the story’s second act.

By the end of Chapter 2 you should have met the stranger characters who hand out side strands. Talk to them when they appear: the “Strangers & Freaks” silver and the five strand-final trophies all build on those meetings, and starting them early spreads the work out.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide:
Finish Chapter 3 and the trophy is yours when its last mission ends. There is no side objective hidden in the chapter requirement — it is purely a story-progress trophy.

Chapter 3 is a good point to check your tracker: if the activity and collectible counts (stunts, vehicles discovered, areas explored) are barely moving, fold a little exploring into your travel between missions instead of fast-travelling everywhere.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide:
Complete Chapter 4 and this trophy pops at the end of its final mission. With the four chapter trophies done, the story stage of the roadmap is nearly complete — only the final mission and the named story missions remain.

Before you push into the finale, open the Missables page and clear every flagged trophy you still can. The finale is the point of no return for several one-time moments, and a quick check now saves a whole second playthrough later.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide:
Finish the final mission and this gold trophy pops. It is the story’s last beat, so it comes after Chapter 4 and after the named story missions — there is no trick to it, just play the finale through to the end.

Do the finale last, not first: the missable trophies, the stranger strands and the big collectible counts are all easier — and in some cases only possible — before the story ends. Keep a manual save from just before the final mission, so you can go back for anything you spot missing afterwards.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide:
Breakfast Run is a named story mission, and this trophy pops when you complete it. Flagged missable because the mission is a one-time story beat: it only comes around once in the story, so play it carefully when it appears and do not rely on coming back to it later.

Keep a save from just before the mission starts. If anything goes wrong mid-mission, reloading that save is far cheaper than replaying the chapter, and it keeps your missable run clean.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide:
Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist and the trophy pops at the end of it. Heist missions are the big set-pieces of the story: expect a planned approach, a loud middle, and a getaway, and follow the mission’s own objectives rather than improvising.

Stock up before the mission starts — ammunition, armour and a fast car for the escape — because heist missions rarely let you shop mid-way. The trophy itself needs nothing extra beyond finishing the job.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide:
Finish the story mission Child’s Play and the trophy unlocks when it ends. It is a straight completion trophy: play the mission through, follow its objectives, and the pop comes on its own.

Child’s Play is one of the named missions the story builds toward, so it arrives in the natural flow of the chapters. If you are tracking your progress, tick it off as you go — the story stage of the roadmap is just the chapter trophies plus these named missions.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide:
Complete the story mission Headliners and the trophy pops when it ends. It is a completion trophy with no extra objective — finish the mission and it is yours.

Headliners sits among the named missions that make up the story stage, so it will come to you as the chapters unfold. Keep your saves tidy around the big missions: a save from before each named mission is the cheapest insurance for the missable trophies nearby.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide:
Finish the story mission VCIA Takedown — the airport job — and the trophy unlocks at its end. The mission’s name says what it is: a takedown at Vice City International Airport, so expect tight spaces, armed resistance and a vehicle-based escape.

Do not confuse this with the separate “Catch Me If You Can” trophy, which is about making an unscheduled departure from VCIA on your own terms. This one only asks you to complete the story mission.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide:
Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory and the trophy pops when it ends. It is the last of the named story-mission trophies: once it is done, the story stage is complete except for the final mission itself.

Operation Savage Glory sounds like a heavy combat mission, so go in prepared — full ammunition, armour, and a plan for the mission’s own checkpoints rather than rushing. Finishing it cleanly is worth more than finishing it fast.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide:
Reach 100% on the game’s own completion checklist — PSN tracks it as a count to 100. This is the gold that gathers almost everything else: the story, the stranger strands, the activities, the collectibles and the exploration all feed into it, so treat it as the last gold before the platinum.

Open the in-game 100% checklist early and check it after every stage of this roadmap: it shows exactly which categories are still short, so you never have to guess what is missing. The usual stragglers are a handful of collectibles, one or two activity types, and a stranger strand you never started — all of them fixable once the checklist names them.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 100). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide:
Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, air time, near misses, drifts and the like — and PSN counts each one toward the 250. This is a volume trophy, not a skill trophy: every stunt you land while driving around Leonida counts, so the number climbs on its own if you drive fast and take ramps whenever you see them.

To grind it deliberately, pick a fast car and a stretch of road with jumps or ramps, and repeat a loop of jumps and drifts. Do not save it all for the end: 250 is a lot in one sitting, but it is nothing spread across a whole playthrough of enthusiastic driving.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 250). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide:
Try each of the game’s 9 activity types once — PSN tracks the count to 9, and the trophy pops when the ninth type is sampled. You do not need to win, finish or master any of them: one honest attempt at each type is enough.

Work through the activities menu one by one early in the game: racing, fishing, the shooting range, drone races, the arcade, bowling, meditation and whatever else the menu lists. Sampling everything early also tells you which activities you enjoy — several of them have their own trophies waiting behind them.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 9). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide:
Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — PSN counts the golds to 42, and the trophy only pops when the last one turns gold. This is the hardest pure-skill trophy on the list, and the one most likely to be your final grind before the platinum.

Go challenge by challenge and learn each one’s rhythm instead of brute-forcing all 42 in a row: the range teaches recoil control, target priority and reload timing, and each weapon handles differently. Start with the challenges that suit your best weapon, bank the easy golds for confidence, and save the hardest ones for when your aim is warm. Retries are free, so a failed run costs nothing but time.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 42). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide:
Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations — PSN counts the locations to 14, and each one needs a win, not just an entry. Drone racing is about the course, not the drone: learn each location’s gates, corners and shortcuts before you push for the win.

Fly a practice lap first at each new location, then race to win. If a location keeps beating you, slow down for the tight gates — a clean line through every gate beats a fast line that misses one. There is no penalty for retrying, so keep at each location until it falls.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 14). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide:
Win 20 different races — PSN counts distinct race wins to 20, so the same race twice only counts once. Race events unlock as new areas of Leonida open up, which is why this one is flagged missable: win each new race as it appears instead of leaving all 20 for the end of the game.

Pick a car that suits the race — grip for tight street circuits, speed for long highway runs — and learn the first two corners of each course, since most races are won or lost there. A win in a fresh race counts toward both this trophy and your stunt and driving totals, so racing early pays twice.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 20). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide:
Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a fishing rival, so the challenge is a head-to-head: out-fish him, not just catch something. Watch the line tension and the fish’s runs — reeling too hard snaps the line, reeling too gently lets the fish escape — and keep steady pressure through the fight.

If you lose, challenge him again: the trophy needs one win, and each attempt teaches you how Cal fishes. Bring your best rod and tackle if the game lets you choose gear, and fish when the challenge is offered rather than putting it off.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide:
Complete one arcade game — any game, any arcade. The trophy asks for a completion, not a high score, so pick the shortest or easiest machine you find and play it through to its end.

Arcades are scattered around Leonida, so try the first one you walk past rather than hunting for a specific title. A quick completion here also counts toward sampling the activity types for “Master of None”.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide:
Complete Andy’s mission strand through to its final mission. Stranger strands are chains: each mission unlocks the next, and this trophy pops when the last one in Andy’s chain is done.

Flagged missable because a strand can be left unfinished if you stop answering the stranger’s calls or move the story past them — start Andy’s strand when you first meet him and finish each mission as it comes, instead of saving the whole chain for after the finale.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide:
Complete Kenton’s mission strand through to its final mission. Like every stranger strand, it is a chain of missions that must be played in order, and the trophy pops at the end of the last one.

Flagged missable for the same reason as the other strand finals: the chain only moves while you keep showing up for Kenton, so do not leave his missions sitting unplayed while the story advances. The title hints the finale involves a boat — expect water, and bring a plan for getting back to shore.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide:
Complete Billy’s mission strand through to its final mission. The strand is a chain — each mission leads to the next — and the trophy unlocks when the final mission is done.

Flagged missable because stranger strands depend on you keeping the chain moving: answer Billy’s calls, play each mission when it opens, and do not let the story run past him. “The Lone Rider” suggests the finale is a solo ride, so expect a long drive and keep a fast bike or car ready.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide:
Complete 8 full mission strands for strangers across Leonida — PSN counts finished strands to 8. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so half-finished chains earn nothing here.

There are five named strand-givers with their own final-mission trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone), and more strangers besides — you need eight finished strands in total, so meet every stranger you find and finish what you start. Keep a note of which strands are done: the tracker’s checklist is the easiest place to tick the five named finals off as you earn them.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 8). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide:
Complete Randy’s mission strand through to its final mission. The strand is a chain of missions in order, and the trophy pops when the last one is finished.

Flagged missable like the other strand finals: the chain only advances while you keep taking Randy’s missions, so play them as they open rather than banking them for later. The name suggests a supply run, so expect cargo, a deadline, and someone trying to take it off you.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide:
Complete Tyrone’s mission strand through to its final mission. Play the chain in order — each mission unlocks the next — and the trophy unlocks at the end of the finale.

Flagged missable like the other strand finals: keep Tyrone’s missions moving while the story is still open to them. “Spin On This!” hints at driving — expect a spin, a chase, or a getaway — so keep a car you trust ready before the final mission starts.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide:
Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida — PSN counts the spots to 18, and the trophy pops when the last one is used. Meditation spots are quiet scenic places: lookouts, beaches, parks and hilltops, spread across the whole map.

Fold this into your exploring: whenever you are near a new area, check whether it holds a meditation spot and use it on the spot, because backtracking to 18 scattered locations at the end is the slow way. The activity itself is calm — sit, breathe, and the spot counts.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 18). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide:
Hunt a unique animal for Bret. This is a one-off hunt, not regular hunting: a single special animal, and the trophy pops when you take it down for Bret. Flagged missable because a unique animal can be spooked, lost or killed wrong — approach carefully and do not rush the shot.

Track the animal patiently, use cover and move slowly, and take the shot only when it is clean. If the hunt goes wrong, reload a save from before you started it rather than chasing the animal across the map. The official description does not name the animal or the place, so expect to find both through Bret himself.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide:
Complete 3 full collectible card sets — PSN counts finished sets to 3. Cards are hidden around Leonida, and a set only counts when every card in it is found, so this is a thoroughness trophy: explore properly, check side rooms and rooftops, and pick up every card you see.

Start collecting from the beginning of the game and keep the cards in your tracker as you find them. Sets are the slow burn of the platinum — the last card of the third set is usually found by sweeping the areas you rushed through during the story, so save a systematic sweep for the cleanup stage.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 3). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide:
Use the WAiNK It activity at 100 locations — PSN counts locations to 100. WAiNK It is a location-based activity, so the work is travel: get to 100 different spots across Leonida and use it at each one.

Treat it as a sightseeing tour: fold WAiNK It stops into your normal travel and your exploration of the 52 areas for “The Goodtime State”, and the two trophies will climb together. A hundred is a lot in one grind, but it is a small detour a hundred times — and detours are the whole point of an open world.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 100). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide:
Complete 50 challenges — PSN counts finished challenges to 50. Challenges are the game’s small goals across every system: driving, shooting, exploring, activities and more, so the count climbs fastest when you play widely instead of grinding one thing.

Open the challenges menu early and skim it: pick off the easy ones first (the ones you are already close to finishing), then work through the rest as you play the other stages. Fifty sounds like a lot until you realise the game is quietly counting half of them while you do everything else.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 50). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide:
Build a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then lose it and escape. Your partner only rides with you during certain stretches of the game, which is why this one is flagged missable: do it while you still have a partner beside you, not after the story has moved on.

Plan it like a heist: pick a quiet area with good escape routes, cause enough trouble to reach four stars, then break line of sight, switch vehicles, and stay out of the search area until the heat dies. A fast car and a hideout nearby make the escape far easier than a long run across open ground.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide:
Rob three shops back-to-back with your partner, without losing your wanted level between them — the chain breaks if the heat drops to zero, so keep the wanted level alive across all three robberies. Flagged missable because it needs your partner beside you, and partners are only available during certain story stretches.

Scout three shops close together first, plan the route, and keep a fast getaway car parked nearby. Hit them quickly one after another: linger in one shop and the police will catch up; dawdle between shops and the wanted level will fade. If the chain breaks, drive off, reset, and try the run again.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide:
Discover 100 different vehicles — PSN counts distinct vehicles to 100. Driving a vehicle you have never driven before counts as a discovery, so the trophy rewards curiosity: try every car, bike, truck and boat you come across instead of sticking to one favourite.

Hunt for variety deliberately: different districts favour different vehicles, so a tour of Leonida’s neighbourhoods, docks, highways and countryside will surface models you would never meet on your usual route. The count climbs alongside the exploration trophy, so do them together.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 100). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide:
Take down five enemies during one single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-motion aiming mode: it gives you time to line up shots, but the window is short, so five takedowns in one use needs a crowded fight, not a duel.

Set it up: find a firefight with plenty of enemies close together, wait until five or more are in view, then trigger Combat Focus and work through them quickly — headshots where you can, and do not waste the window on reloading. If the focus runs out at four, disengage, find another crowd, and try again.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide:
Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport — in plain terms, steal a plane and take off without clearance. Flagged missable because the airport is a guarded, high-heat location and the opportunity is a one-off stunt: go in with a plan, not on a whim.

Pick a plane near a runway, expect police attention the moment you climb in, and take off fast — a long taxi gives security time to catch you. Once you are airborne, the trophy should pop; if it does not, land somewhere quiet and try a different aircraft or runway.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide:
Deal with Rhino tanks — the description’s joke is the clue: “Kinda hot in these Rhinos” means you will be facing military armour, and it will be hot. Flagged missable because Rhino encounters are tied to high-wanted-level chaos and specific story moments, so be ready when one shows up instead of running from it.

Rhinos are slow but nearly unstoppable head-on: use sticky bombs, heavy weapons or high ground, and never stand in front of the cannon. Keep your distance, hit the weak spots, and have an escape vehicle ready — surviving a Rhino is the whole challenge.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide:
Rob a jewelry store without being detected — the whole job must be silent, from entry to exit. Flagged missable because a blown attempt can lock the store down: scout first, go in quiet, and if you are spotted, leave and reset rather than shooting your way out.

Plan the route before you enter: know where the staff and cameras are, move slowly, take only what you need, and leave the way you came. A clean run needs patience more than speed — one careless step is the difference between a silent robbery and a siren.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide:
Rob five bank vaults and escape from each one — PSN counts completed vault robberies to 5, and each one needs the escape, not just the break-in. Bank vaults are the big robberies: plan the approach, crack the vault, grab the cash, and get out before the response arrives.

Treat each vault as its own heist: scout the bank, park a fast car nearby, and know your escape route before you go in. Five successful escapes is a campaign, not a single night — spread them across the crime stage and let the money pile up toward the laundering trophy.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 5). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide:
Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks run set routes around Leonida, so the job is an ambush: find a truck on the road, stop it, crack it open, take the cash, and get away before the police arrive.

Block the truck with your own vehicle or force it to stop, then deal with the guards quickly — the longer the stop takes, the bigger the response. Grab the money and leave fast: a clean escape matters as much as the robbery itself, and a slow getaway turns a payday into a chase.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide:
Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — PSN counts visited areas to 52, and the trophy pops when the last one is ticked off. Leonida is a whole state, not just Vice City: beaches, swamps, small towns, highways and countryside all count as their own areas.

Do it as a road trip rather than a chore: drive the state border to border, stop at every named place, and let the other exploration trophies (vehicles, meditation spots, WAiNK It locations) ride along. The in-game map is your checklist — the areas you have never visited are the gaps, and the gaps are the trip.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 52). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide:
Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs — PSN counts gangs hit to 9, so one operation per gang, nine gangs in total. Each gang runs its own rackets in its own territory, so the work is as much finding them as robbing them.

Map the gangs first: learn which crew controls which turf, then hit one operation in each territory and move on. Expect armed guards at every site and a response afterwards, so bring a fast car and an exit plan — nine clean hits beats nine messy ones.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 9). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide:
Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — find the bar or beach spot on Ocean Beach where you can sit with a drink and the sea in front of you, and take the moment. Flagged missable because it is a quiet, one-time-feeling moment: it is easy to walk straight past it while chasing the next mission.

Slow down for it deliberately: go to Ocean Beach, find the cocktail spot, and enjoy the view. It is the calmest trophy on the list, and a good palate-cleanser between the loud ones — the game is telling you to stop and look at the place you have been running around.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide:
Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom glass and out onto the street. The “classic style” is the joke: this is the old-school GTA showroom smash, done on purpose.

Pick a showroom, get a car inside or lined up at the glass, and floor it through the window. Expect alarms and a wanted level on the way out, so have your escape ready before you go in — the trophy pops on the smash, but you still have to get away.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide:
Follow through at the Kolt & Associates’ bowling alley — in other words, play a proper game of bowling there. “Follow-through” is the bowling term for completing your throw, so the trophy is about playing the game, not just walking into the alley.

Go to the Kolt & Associates alley, start a game, and bowl your frames. You do not need a perfect game — just play it through. It is a gentle trophy and a good break between the grindy ones, and it counts toward sampling the activity types too.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide:
A partnership with mass appeal — a story-gated partnership moment, and the kind of trophy whose meaning only lands when you reach it. Flagged missable because it is tied to a particular point in the partnership: do it when the moment comes, not after the story has moved on.

The official description is deliberately vague, and this guide will not pretend to know the exact scene: watch for a partnership milestone the game clearly signposts — a shared success the world notices — and lean into it when it appears. If you are chasing the platinum, treat every big partnership beat as potentially this trophy.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide:
Make choices — PSN tracks them to 500, so this is a long count that builds across the whole game. Every decision the game offers, big or small, adds to it: dialogue choices, approach choices, moral choices. Flagged missable because choices can only be made while the game is offering them, and a playthrough that rushes past every prompt will run short.

The honest advice is to play attentively: stop and choose at every prompt instead of mashing through, take the side content that offers decisions, and let the count grow. Five hundred is a lot, but it is the sum of a whole playthrough of paying attention — and it pairs naturally with the stranger strands, which are full of choices.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 500). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide:
“Second time’s the charm” — succeed at something on your second try. This is the retry trophy: fail an attempt at a challenge or activity, then succeed on the very next attempt, and it pops. Flagged missable because it is easy to accidentally make it impossible: if you reload a save after every failure, you never have a genuine second try.

The practical way to earn it is to let a failure stand: pick a challenge you might fail once, fail it honestly, then win the retry immediately. Do not save-scum around it — the trophy wants the failure and the comeback in that order.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide:
“What the hell just happened?” — witness something strange. This is the game’s oddity trophy: a weird event, a strange sighting, something out of the ordinary that you have to be in the right place at the right time to see. Flagged missable because strange events are rare by nature, and you can play a whole game without stumbling into one.

The official description does not say what the event is, and this guide will not invent a location for it. The honest approach is to explore the odd corners of Leonida — the remote places, the late-night spots, the things that look out of place — and to keep an eye out while you do the other stages. Strange things tend to find players who wander.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide:
Bowl someone over with a melee drive-by — hit a pedestrian with a melee swing from a moving vehicle. The bowling pun is the method: you are the ball, the person is the pin, and the car is the lane.

Drive slowly through a crowded area, wait until someone is close beside the car, and swing as you pass. Speed makes it harder, not easier — a slow roll-by gives you time to aim the swing. One clean knockdown is all it takes, so do not keep swinging after it pops.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide:
Earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts — PSN counts the laundered total to $250,000. Marked bills come from robberies and heists: dirty money that needs washing before you can spend it, and your contacts take a cut for cleaning it.

Feed the system steadily: every robbery and vault job produces marked bills, so launder them through your contacts as you earn them instead of letting a pile sit dirty. The $250,000 is cumulative across the whole game, and the crime stage’s five bank vaults and the cartel heist will get you most of the way there.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 250000). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide:
Spend $100,000 across all shops — PSN counts total spending to $100,000, and every shop counts: clothes, weapons, food, car parts, whatever the game sells. It is cumulative across the whole playthrough, so it climbs while you live in Leonida.

Do not force it early: a hundred thousand is a lot of shopping before you are rich, and the crime stage will make you rich. Spend on the things that help — weapons, armour, cars, clothes you actually want — and check the total in the tracker as the money flows in. By the cleanup stage, the last few thousand is a shopping trip, not a grind.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 100000). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide:
Purchase all 8 garage properties — PSN counts the garages to 8, and the trophy pops when the last deed is yours. Garages are bought with clean money, so this one is really a savings trophy: earn well, launder what needs laundering, and buy each garage as you can afford it.

Garages also store the vehicles you discover for “Whip It Good”, so buying them early pays twice — a place to keep the cars you find, and progress toward this trophy. Check property listings as you travel: the eight garages are spread across Leonida, and the expensive ones will wait until the crime stage has paid out.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 8). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide:
Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — PSN counts registered vehicles to 10. The app is the game’s vehicle service, so the job is to bring it ten different vehicles and register each one.

Use the variety you are already discovering for “Whip It Good”: every new vehicle you drive is a candidate for the app. Register them as you find them rather than hunting for ten at the end, and the trophy will be done before the collectible stage is.
trophies.sources: Official list: Exophase (name, description, grade). PSNProfiles (PSN progress count: 10). Guide: our own advice from the official description — not yet checked in the game.
